harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, cron access is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow (cronie honors cron.allow as an exclusive whitelist when present, and pre-existing /etc/cron.deny was empty so it plays no role). Created the opsadmin user, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin, and verified enforcement both before and after a full node reboot: unlisted users are rejected by `crontab` ("not allowed to use this program"), while opsadmin and root can still create/read crontabs. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol with boot_id proof of an actual reboot and post-restart re-verification of crond health and the cron access restriction.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline cron config on node1 (no /etc/cron.allow, empty /etc/cron.deny, cronie/crontabs installed, crond active)
Created opsadmin user on node1
Created temporary crontestuser to establish an unrestricted baseline (both opsadmin and crontestuser could schedule cron jobs)
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' (root:root, 0644)
Verified via runuser that crontestuser is denied by crontab while opsadmin succeeds
Cleaned up test crontabs and removed the temporary crontestuser
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline (crond active, cron.allow content)
Rebooted node1 via a backgrounded delayed `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart: crond active, /etc/cron.allow intact, opsadmin can schedule cron, a fresh non-listed user (finalcheckuser) is denied
Removed finalcheckuser test account

evidence.requirement: Baseline: cron unrestricted before change (opsadmin and a normal user can both use crontab)
evidence.summary: No /etc/cron.allow existed and /etc/cron.deny was empty; both opsadmin and crontestuser successfully installed crontabs (exit 0)

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin allowed to schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.allow with 'root' and 'opsadmin'; direct runuser test shows crontestuser denied ('not allowed to use this program') while opsadmin succeeds

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of verification artifacts, final state confirmation
evidence.summary: Removed test crontabs and crontestuser account; /etc/cron.allow still contains only root and opsadmin, crond active

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart — healthy baseline before reboot
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d), crond active, cron.allow content confirmed

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart — acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded delayed reboot command acknowledged successfully (exit 0) before the node went unreachable

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart — changed boot identity proves actual restart
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot (timeouts/reset), then reachable again with new boot_id ac840178-c701-4bc7-8677-d1b58ac5e2ce, differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart — post-restart recovery of required service and configuration
evidence.summary: After reboot: crond active, /etc/cron.allow still root+opsadmin only, opsadmin can create a crontab, and a newly created unlisted user is denied by crontab
